prior: let past verdicts move a page up, and measure it before turning it on (PLAN J17; 6.2-6.4).

The feedback prior is off by default. Two judged queries are the whole evidence here: "runbook"
found the release runbook, and a later query, "deploy", wanted the same page but met the release
notes first. kb eval replays each query as of its own time and without its own feedback, so the
runbook's first verdict can lift the second query; it can never lift the first one.

  $ kb init --model fake:8
  created location $WORK/proj/.kb
  created store "default" in $WORK/proj (model fake:8)

  $ kb add $WORK/notes/runbook.md
  added data/runbook.md (2 chunks)
  $ kb add $WORK/notes/notes.md
  added data/notes.md (2 chunks)
  $ kb add $WORK/notes/backup.md
  added data/backup.md (2 chunks)

The synonyms file makes "deploy" and "release" the same word.

  $ write .kb/stores/default/synonyms.txt @synonyms

First query, then the verdict.

  $ kb search runbook --mode fts --caller agent
  search 1 · 2 hits
  [1] data/runbook.md · updated 2026-02-01
  Release runbook: How the release is rolled out.

  [2] data/runbook.md › (intro) · updated 2026-02-01
  Release runbook › (intro)
  # Release runbook

  Roll out each release in stages and watch the dashboards.
  search_id=1
  $ kb feedback --last 1 --useful --caller agent
  recorded: search 1 rank 1 useful=1 (newest search for agent, (time): "runbook")

Verdicts count only for searches after them, and the log keeps whole seconds: move the clock on
between a verdict and the next search.

  $ env KB_HARNESS_NOW=+5m
  $ kb search deploy --mode fts --caller agent
  search 2 · 4 hits
  [1] data/notes.md · updated 2026-02-02
  Release notes: What changed in each release.

  [2] data/runbook.md · updated 2026-02-01
  Release runbook: How the release is rolled out.

  [3] data/notes.md › (intro) · updated 2026-02-02
  Release notes › (intro)
  # Release notes

  Release notes list every release, its date and its release owner.

  [4] data/runbook.md › (intro) · updated 2026-02-01
  Release runbook › (intro)
  # Release runbook

  Roll out each release in stages and watch the dashboards.
  search_id=2
  $ kb feedback 2 2 --useful --caller agent
  recorded: search 2 rank 2 useful=1
  $ env KB_HARNESS_NOW=+10m

Off by default: explain shows no prior line and the notes lead, and eval scores the log as it is
(the runbook is rank 2 for "deploy", so MRR is 0.750).

  $ kb explain deploy --mode fts
  ~ explain "deploy" · mode fts · k 8 · settings [0-9a-f]{12}
  ...
  synonyms: deploy = release
  lists: fts 4 rows · vec 0 rows · 4 candidates
  ...
  ~ #1  rrf [0-9.]+  data/notes.md  \[returned as hit #1\]
  ...
  ~ #2  rrf [0-9.]+  data/runbook.md  \[returned as hit #2\]
  ...

  $ kb eval --mode fts --save-baseline
  ~ eval · mode fts · k 8 · settings [0-9a-f]{12}
  searches: 2 logged · 2 useful · 0 --none · 0 not-useful only · 0 unjudged · 0 with opens
  queries=2 hit@8=1.000 [1.000, 1.000] mrr=0.750 [0.500, 1.000] ndcg@8=0.815 [0.631, 1.000]
  ...
  ~ saved baseline "default" \(2 queries, settings [0-9a-f]{12}\) to \$WORK/proj/\.kb/stores/default/eval/default\.json

Try the prior against that baseline (prior.min_judged=1 because the log is tiny).

  $ kb eval --mode fts --set prior.enabled=true --set prior.min_judged=1 --compare
  ~ compare · baseline "default" \(.*\)
  ~         now \(mode fts · settings [0-9a-f]{12} · fake:8 · 3 entries\) · k 8
  ...
  chunk: 2 paired queries (0 only in the baseline, 0 only now)
  ...
    mrr          0.750    1.000   +0.250  [+0.000, +0.500]  1/0/1     1.000
  ...
  entry: 2 paired queries (0 only in the baseline, 0 only now)
  ...
  ~ small sample: 2 paired queries < eval.min_judged 30; .*
  prior: active in 1/2 replays · query memory placed hits in 0 (each replay as of its search's time, without its own query's feedback)

The first query could not use the prior (nothing was known before it), the second did: the
runbook, rank 2 without the prior, is rank 1 with it (+0.250 MRR). Two queries are a demo, not
evidence; the small-sample line says so.

Query memory is the second switch the README names.

  $ kb eval --mode fts --set prior.enabled=true --set prior.query_memory=true --set prior.min_judged=1 --compare
  ~ compare · baseline "default" \(.*\)
  ...
  ~ small sample: 2 paired queries < eval.min_judged 30; .*
  ~ prior: active in .* replays · query memory placed hits in .* \(.*\)

explain shows the prior term for the same setting.

  $ kb explain deploy --mode fts --set prior.enabled=true --set prior.min_judged=1
  ~ explain "deploy" · mode fts · k 8 · settings [0-9a-f]{12}
  ...
  prior: active · 2/1 judged searches · half-life 90 days · max boost 0.2
  lists: fts 4 rows · vec 0 rows · 4 candidates
  ...
  ~ #1  rrf [0-9.]+  data/runbook.md  \[returned as hit #1\]
  ...
  ~     prior  x1\.0[0-9]+
  ...
  ~ #2  rrf [0-9.]+  data/notes.md  \[returned as hit #2\]
  ...
      prior  x1.0000
  ...
